Include payload digests, destinations, marker targets and any bounded\\n   release-only integration in that plan.\\n2. Run the transition gate check for the intended target state.\\n3. Obtain the accountable human's decision on the selected release record\\n   (RLS). Reuse a matching decision already supplied.\\n   For complete delivery, the same response explicitly covers its listed external\\n   actions. Retain the actual human, decision reference and reviewed plan digest.\\n   Do not rewrite the plan when public observations arrive; retain them separately.\\n4. Retain a rejection reason when applicable.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --checkpoint transition --target TARGET --json\\n```\\n\\nUse `released` or `rejected` for `TARGET`, according to the proposed decision.\\nThe evaluator determines legality. A passed check does not supply approval.\\n\\n**Completion:** The release decision is explicit, or remains pending.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Record the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#record-the-release-decision-when-required) records that decision. Execute listed delivery actions\\nunder the same complete-release authorization when their conditions still match.\\nOtherwise obtain only the exact external authority that is missing.\\n\\n### Record the release decision, when required\\n\\n**Inputs:** The human's exact decision and unchanged release inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected release record (RLS) receives the\\n  permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated release record (RLS), retained through\\n  authorized Git actions.\\n- **Transient working material:** The applied result and current next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Compare the current release inputs with the human's reviewed inputs.\\n2. Preview the selected transition.\\n3. Apply the same command when its gates pass and effects match the decision.\\n4. Inspect the release record (RLS) and report the actual resulting state.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor rejection, add `--reason \\\"RLS-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to both transition\\ncommands. Related verification records (VREC) and work orders (WO) are not\\ntransitioned automatically.\\n\\nFor a complete-release decision, use the existing `--reason` input to retain the\\nactual human decision reference and reviewed delivery-plan path and SHA-256.\\nThis is retained evidence of the supplied decision, not permission derived by\\nparsing arbitrary reason text. Compare the candidate's observed behavior with each acceptance criterion.\\n2. Map every required check to its actual evidence file and pass condition.\\n3. Confirm that the evidence applies to the selected candidate and environment.\\n4. Run missing checks using the verification contract's (VER) commands or\\n   manual procedure. Retain their actual results.\\n5. Record each criterion as passed, failed, or not assessed, with its reason.\\n6. Retain material findings and their resolution with the verification evidence.\\n7. For a defect requiring implementation changes, identify a work order that\\n   covers the correction and is eligible for execution. Follow the recovery\\n   rules under \\u201cIf a procedure is blocked.\\u201d A completed work order does not\\n   become executable again because verification found a defect.\\n8. After the authorized correction, establish the new candidate identity and\\n   reassess the affected criteria against evidence for that candidate.\\n\\n**Harness command:** None for the substantive assessment. Use the check\\ncommands and manual assessments defined in the verification contracts (VER).\\nHarness validation alone does not prove the required behavior.\\n\\n**Completion:** Every required criterion has evidence or a visible gap.\\nFailures and missing checks are not reported as passes.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare the verification record](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#prepare-the-verification-record) binds the retained evidence to a verification record\\n(VREC). [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) uses it for the human's assessment.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"78a405625bfb24107f4b8f4f09ad84942d5710c55b27d58f3114da5f40688c3b\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-the-verification-record\", \"title\": \"Prepare the verification record\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-the-verification-record\", \"start_line\": 108, \"end_line\": 169, \"content\": \"### Prepare the verification record\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact candidate, selected work orders (WO), their verification\\ncontracts (VER), retained evidence, and existing preparation authority.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** One new verification record (VREC) in `ready` when\\n  capture is required and succeeds. Related work-order (WO) states do not change.\\n- **Retained files:** The generated evaluator evidence and candidate snapshot\\n  or export required by the capture procedure.\\n- **Transient working material:** The capture result and inspected output paths.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. If a suitable verification record (VREC) already exists, inspect it and\\n   continue to [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision). Do not duplicate an interrupted successful capture.\\n2. Confirm preparation authority under every selected work order's (WO)\\n   approval. Reuse it while the scope and inputs match.\\n3. Select an unused `VREC-ID` after checking the repository's local Git refs.\\n4. Confirm the domain and actual record and evidence destinations. Keep all\\n   generated writes within the authorized preparation scope.\\n5. Establish a clean committed candidate using authorized local Git actions.\\n   Retain its full commit ID. Do not discard unrelated changes to obtain it.\\n6. Run the capture command with each selected work order (WO), every declared\\n   verification contract (VER), and each retained evidence file.\\n7. Read the generated record and evaluator evidence. Confirm the candidate\\n   commit, selected IDs, evidence digests, and `ready` state.\\n8. Retain generated records and evidence in a later authorized governance\\n   commit. Preserve the earlier candidate commit that the record assesses.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl capture-verification REPO --id VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --verification VER-ID --evidence EVIDENCE-PATH --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order`, `--verification`, and `--evidence` for every selected\\ninput. `EVIDENCE-PATH` is a repository-relative file, not a directory or an\\nindex whose links will be followed automatically. Capture writes immediately\\nafter its checks; it has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\nIf an unchanged rebase leaves an earlier ready record bound to the old\\ncandidate, use [Refresh verification after an unchanged rebase](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#refresh-verification-after-an-unchanged-rebase).\\nA verified source or changed relevant inputs cannot use that shortcut.\\n\\nIf preserving local edits requires the supported committed-candidate route,\\nuse `--candidate-commit COMMIT` with `--test-command EXECUTABLE ARGUMENTS`.\\nPut `--test-command` last. That route tests the named commit in a temporary\\ncheckout; use its actual results and returned record, not results from the\\nuncommitted edits.\\n\\n**Completion:** A ready verification record (VREC) binds the selected candidate\\nand evidence, or capture reports a specific refusal. Preparation is not verification.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) presents the exact record and evidence for the human decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"34e77e503346373221eaa0bb46e970ee738ce6a5eebbfdece9ba6e8ee36450a1\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-lifecycle-native27-20261010\\\\codex-221\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"892ec2fedefc272f6bc2580268395e487f392cf5d92a3ea81fac015761bc87a8\", \"bytes\": 8641, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"verification-coverage\", \"title\": \"Verification coverage\", \"anchor\": \"verification-coverage\", \"start_line\": 117, \"end_line\": 123, \"content\": \"## Verification coverage\\n\\nA verification record (VREC) MUST bind one or more\\nwork orders (WO), all their declared verification contracts (VER), retained\\nevidence, and one exact clean candidate commit. Preparing a verification\\nrecord (VREC) does not change its state to `verified`.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d0359e722c997b266376b6644404fca0db87d8718a79d2f2503aca0669936adf\"}, {\"heading\": \"release-coverage\", \"title\": \"Release coverage\", \"anchor\": \"release-coverage\", \"start_line\": 132, \"end_line\": 148, \"content\": \"## Release coverage\\n\\nA release record (RLS) MUST bind one release contract\\n(REL), one exact candidate commit, and eligible verification records (VREC)\\nat that same commit. Its released-work set MUST equal the combined set of\\nwork orders (WO) covered by those verification records (VREC). Governance\\nwork is included only when the release record (RLS) explicitly includes\\nverification records (VREC) that provide eligible coverage for that work.\\nA related record or dashboard cannot add work to a release.\\n\\nThis model describes the readable record structure. This release's\\n`prepare-release` procedure is narrower: it requires one final verification\\nrecord covering the complete released-work set. When earlier records cover\\nseparate parts, prepare and verify a record for the exact combined candidate\\nthrough [Verify the outcome](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#procedure) before using that release procedure. Do not\\nassemble or edit a release record by hand to bypass the preparation checks.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"93f737690c97f39827a714e344537ef3f19359a646142a3e49f5b76ab4ffbabb\"}]}]}\r\n",

A preview never changes graph state. Actor strings\\nare synthetic test inputs, not authenticated human consent.\\n\\nThe digest binds project/context versions, all selected revision IDs, retained\\nsnapshot, exact command/file inputs, principal and released evaluator identity.\\nMode and operation key are excluded from the preview binding, but included in\\nthe accepted request digest used for principal-scoped retry lookup.\\n\\n## Permitted file effects\\n\\n| Action | Permitted effects in the disposable projection |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| check / preflight / validate | No file writes |\\n| transition | Only selected newly authored artifacts and evaluator sidecars declared by their records |\\n| decide | Selected new decision and its explicitly linked rehearsal risk |\\n| raise-risk | New risk and optional paired decision at released domain paths |\\n| handoff | Declared bounded file inputs within the selected work order's scope; released handoff packet and evaluator evidence |\\n| capture-verification | New VREC and its released evaluator sidecar |\\n| prepare-release | New RLS and its released evaluator sidecar |\\n\\nHandoff first uses the released procedure's fixed `evidence` preparation command,\\nthen `check --checkpoint handoff --from-git`. It exposes no arbitrary evidence\\ncommand. File inputs cannot alter formal records, harness selection/instructions,\\nGit configuration, hooks, or executables used by the service. The service never\\nruns source tests. The local qualification runner supplies observed test evidence.\\n\\nThe adapter enumerates every regular file before and after the operation. It\\nrejects deletions, links, unexpected paths, missing sidecars, imported-record\\nchanges and evaluator failure before opening an acceptance transaction.\\n\\n## Snapshots and Git\\n\\nEach accepted operation retains an immutable complete snapshot: exact file bytes,\\nself-contained Git history and its source/test-candidate identities. Content\\ndigests bind the snapshot to the resulting baseline. Context heads, artifact\\nrevisions, snapshot and receipt share one database transaction. Temporary Git\\nrepositories are discarded after the result is accepted or refused.\\n\\nCapture first commits the exact input projection as test candidate P. P excludes\\nthe new VREC. The output retains the input hosted baseline B, source fixture S,\\nP and evaluator identity. Actual implementation candidate C is recorded separately\\nby qualification. Subsequent commits never alter the candidate stored in a VREC.\\n\\nExport selects an immutable baseline, checks its complete snapshot and Git bundle,\\nand returns exact bounded bytes. The installed client writes only to a new explicit\\ndestination and leaves an incomplete marker until every file hash is checked.\\nNo export writes to or synchronizes an authoritative repository.\\n\\n## Bounds and failure categories\\n\\nKeep 4 MiB requests, 2 MiB responses, 1 MiB individual file inputs, two concurrent\\nprojections, 120-second evaluator calls and 10,000 retained artifact revisions.\\nA pilot snapshot/export that exceeds the response bound is refused atomically.\\nRetained complete snapshots have a separate explicit project count bound of 128.\\nThis is a small private pilot, not an unbounded document store.\\n\\nBoundary/malformed requests, stale inputs, evaluator refusals, invalid output and\\nunknown transport outcomes remain distinct. Read the operation receipt after a\\nlost reply. A changed request under the same accepted key is a conflict. The\\nservice does not automatically rerun a mutation at a newer version.\\n\\n## Bounded Cypher reads\\n\\nThe existing `cypher` MCP/HTTP read selects one exact view. Its request uses the\\nread schema, not the lifecycle command schema. Read the public labels and\\nproperties in [the physical representation](../../docs/notes/hosted-artifact-graph.md#physical-representation)\\nbefore selecting a query. `Artifact` and `Revision` are distinct public labels.\\n\\nThe admitted form has one `MATCH` or `OPTIONAL MATCH` path, labelled nodes,\\noptional parameterized property comparisons, `RETURN`, and a numeric `LIMIT`.\\nFor example, with `parameters` containing a selected artifact ID under `artifact`:\\n\\n```cypher\\nMATCH (r:Revision) WHERE r.artifact_id = $artifact RETURN r.artifact_id AS id, r.status AS status LIMIT 10\\n```\\n\\nUse the response's completeness fields with the requested row/byte/depth budget.\\nThis example supplies no project filter: the service binds the selected project\\nand view. Unlabelled nodes, `WITH`, aggregation and arbitrary database syntax are\\nnot part of this small public read form. A rejected query has not completed a read.\\nKeep the exact refusal; consult the documented form before constructing another\\nrequest. Do not weaken query admission or bypass it through a direct database call.\\n\"}\r\n",

Inspect the selected work order (WO), verification record (VREC), or release\\n   record (RLS) with the command below.\\n2. Name the action: for example, create a pull request, merge, prepare a\\n   release, tag, publish, or deploy.\\n3. Identify the full candidate commit or immutable release identity.\\n4. Identify the exact target repository and ref, registry, or deployment environment.\\n5. Read the repository's instructions for that delivery action.\\n6. Select the matching procedure or a complete alternative declared by the\\n   evaluator. Resolve an ambiguous destination with the requester.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact ARTIFACT-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse a work order (WO), verification record (VREC), or release record (RLS)\\nas `ARTIFACT-ID`. Selection changes no lifecycle state.\\n\\n**Completion:** One delivery action and target are explicit. Selecting a path\\ndoes not authorize or perform its external action.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare the delivery package](DELIVER_RESULT.md#prepare-the-delivery-package), [Obtain the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#obtain-the-release-decision-when-required), [Record the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#record-the-release-decision-when-required), [Confirm authority for the external action](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-authority-for-the-external-action), [Perform the authorized delivery](DELIVER_RESULT.md#perform-the-authorized-delivery), [Confirm the delivery result](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-the-delivery-result) prepare, authorize, perform, and confirm that action.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"3c62d9982634dc649143dfbaa6d84299d868a5b1f9f4d18861c99d673da2f01d\"}]}]}\r\n",
